title: The Week Support Went Quiet
subtitle: Automation coverage climbed, tickets dropped, and one release stole the show.

sections.label: Opening
sections.title: The Week Support Went Quiet
sections.subtitle: Automation coverage climbed, tickets dropped, and one release stole the show. Compiled from the week's own records.
chips: Demo data — replace with your feed
sections.narration: Good evening. Zop AI, weekly briefing, week forty — Monday the twenty-eighth of September through Sunday the fourth of October. This week, the machines did the boring parts: twelve thousand tasks automated, and support finally went quiet. Sit back, sir. The numbers are rather pleasing.

sections.label: Scoreboard
sections.heading: The week in numbers
sections.narration: First, the scoreboard. Twelve thousand eight hundred forty-seven tasks automated — up eighteen percent. Average response time, one point nine seconds. Support tickets: two hundred fourteen. That is down thirty-one percent. And uptime held at ninety-nine point nine eight percent. Four numbers, one conclusion: the platform is pulling its weight.

items.note: Live Tuesday. Routes 4 of 5 tickets with no human touch.

items.name: Slack connector
items.note: Live Thursday. Alert digests in three workspaces already.

items.name: Multilingual summaries

items.name: Audit log export
items.note: Schema migration needs a redesign. Watch this one.

sections.narration: Now, the build board. Smart Triage version two shipped on Tuesday, and it routes tickets without waking a human four times out of five. The Slack connector shipped Thursday. Multilingual summaries are at sixty-eight percent, on track. Audit log export, though, sits at forty-five percent and is flagged at risk — the one to watch.

sections.label: Tickets per day
sections.heading: Tickets handled per day
sections.caption: Human-touch tickets, Monday through Sunday. The slope is the point.
sections.narration: Here is the week's best chart. Tickets handled per day, Monday through Sunday. Fifty-eight. Forty-one. Thirty-six. Twenty-two. Fourteen. Nine. And Sunday, nine. Every step down is an hour a human got back. That slope is the entire business case, drawn in one line.

sections.label: Where hours went
sections.heading: Where the automation hours went
sections.caption: Share of automated task hours by department, week 40.
sections.narration: Where did the automation hours go? Support takes forty-two percent. Sales ops, twenty-seven. Reporting, nineteen. Internal tooling, twelve. Support still leads, but sales ops grew fastest — that is the quiet expansion to watch next quarter.

sections.label: The week
sections.heading: The week, day by day

events.text: Data pipeline hiccup — fixed before lunch. Forty minutes, no data lost.
Smart Triage v2 goes live for all customers.
Audit review passes with zero findings.
Slack connector ships; three workspaces adopt on day one.
Northwind client demo — they signed before the coffee went cold.

sections.narration: The week, day by day. Monday: a data pipeline hiccup, fixed before lunch — forty minutes, no data lost. Tuesday: Smart Triage version two goes live. Wednesday: the slowest day, and quietly the most important — the audit review passed with zero findings. Thursday: the Slack connector ships. Friday: the Northwind demo. They signed before the coffee went cold.

sections.label: Wins & blockers
sections.heading: Wins and blockers

wins.note: From 71% last week — biggest single-week jump this quarter.
First clean audit since the platform launched.
Largest deal of the quarter, closed five days after first demo.

blockers.note: Schema migration trickier than planned. New design lands Monday.
Vendor-side cap. Workaround in place, queued requests under 1%.

sections.narration: The wins: automation coverage crossed eighty percent, the audit passed clean, and Northwind signed. The blockers: the audit log export slipped — the schema migration is trickier than planned — and a rate limit on the CRM connector side, workaround already in place. Two blockers, both owned, both dated.

sections.label: Next week
sections.heading: Next week's plan

items.text: Audit log export: new schema in, hard deadline Thursday
Sales ops connector graduates from pilot to production

sections.note: If all three land, week 41 closes with automation coverage past 90%.
sections.narration: Next week: the audit log export gets its new schema, with a hard deadline of Thursday. Multilingual summaries hit public beta. And the sales ops connector graduates from pilot to production. If those three land, week forty-one ends with automation coverage past ninety percent. That, sir, is the plan.

sections.label: Close
sections.heading: End of briefing
sections.message: Numbers up. Tickets down. One signature on the wall.
sections.narration: That closes week forty. Numbers up, tickets down, one signature on the wall. The full data behind every figure lives in the report pack — and next week's briefing will be waiting, right here. Until then… the machines have it from here.
